title: dotsteward hosts/<name>.toml
description: What the instance says about one machine, schema version 1. The file name is the machine name: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$. Only that machine writes the file. Unknown keys are errors.
$comment: Readers interpret the keyword subset of workstation.schema.json.

system.description: The Nix system of the machine, one of nix.systems.

profile.description: The profile this machine runs, one of profiles.names.

platform.description: The operating system and its version, for example ubuntu-24.04.

declined.description: What this machine never takes, kept across a reinstall with the same name.

holds.description: What this machine holds back, by kind and name. `component:<name>`, or the bare name as earlier releases wrote it, is a component hold, which the owner writes: the pins of the component take no version from `version` on, and on this machine its apt packages keep the installed upstream version and take only its Debian revisions while below it. `pin:<id>` is a pin hold, which `dotsteward upgrade` writes when a move of that pin went red here: the pin does not take `version` until upstream calls a newer one the latest, or `upgrade --retry-held`. Every machine honours them, since the shared lock reaches them all.

apt.description: The apt settings of this machine.

gated.description: The kernel and driver classes only `dotsteward upgrade` moves.

enable.description: false leaves those classes to apt on this machine.

tag.description: A tag; the prefixes machine: and no: are reserved for the framework.
